name: Projective Splat Rasterization with Depth Optimization
definition: A rasterization technique for point-based rendering that uses the inverse of a projective mapping matrix to transform screen coordinates back to object space for kernel evaluation, while simultaneously computing window-space depth values via linear interpolation of homogeneous coordinates.
summary: Projective Splat Rasterization with Depth Optimization is a point-based rendering technique that avoids explicit matrix inversion by using adjoint matrices and optimizes depth computation by embedding window-space depth directly into homogeneous interpolation weights.
